entries.title: Free FK cluster power sums
entries.statement: For a finite graph G with N vertices and an FK edge configuration omega, let S_j(omega)=sum_C |C|^j over every open cluster C, including isolated vertices. Thus S_1=N. Cluster sizes are random under the FK law; independent cluster colouring does not make the sizes independent.
assumptions: open connected components including isolated vertices

entries.title: DRAFT: exact free Potts field cumulants
entries.statement: AUTHOR-DERIVED FINITE IDENTITY, pending independent proof admission. For a nonempty finite graph, integer q>=2, finite beta>=0, free-boundary zero-field Potts weights exp(beta sum_e 1{same colour}), let X=sum_x(1{sigma_x=1}-1/q), P(h)=N^(-1)log E[exp(hX)], and S_j=sum_C |C|^j under free FK with p=1-exp(-beta). With a2=(q-1)/q^2, a3=(q-1)(q-2)/q^3, a4=(q-1)(q^2-6q+6)/q^4, P second and third derivatives at zero are a2 E[S2]/N and a3 E[S3]/N. The fourth is (a4 E[S4]+3 a2^2 Var(S2))/N. No uniform thermodynamic remainder follows.
assumptions: free FK expectations at zero field

entries.title: DRAFT: obstruction to averaging conditional fourth cumulants
entries.statement: FINITE DIAGNOSTIC, pending independent proof admission. Under the free, zero-field finite Potts hypotheses of the exact cumulant identity, averaging conditional fourth cumulants misses 3 a2^2 Var(S2)/N, a nonnegative term. Exact spin/FK enumeration on six graphs with q=2,3,4,5 and exp(beta)=1,2,4 found 40 failures in 72 cases when this term was dropped, including two wrong quartic signs. The complete identity had zero failures. This does not prove a critical transition.

entries.title: DRAFT: quantitative cubic stationary-minimum exclusion
entries.statement: AUTHOR-DERIVED CONDITIONAL LEMMA, pending independent proof admission. Let r0,b>0,C>=0 and differentiable F(m)=a m^2-b_t m^3+R(m) on [0,r0], with b_t>=b, |R(m)|<=C m^4 and |R prime(m)|<=4C m^3. No interior stationary point with F(m)<=F(0)=0 can have 0<m<min(r0,b/(6C)) when C>0; when C=0 no such interior point exists. Substituting stationarity yields F(m)>=b m^3/2-3C m^4.
assumptions: all bounds on a common interval

entries.title: UNPROVED: uniform Potts scalar-potential input
entries.statement: MISSING INPUT, not asserted true. Fix integer q,d>=3, zero-field unit-coupling nearest-neighbour Potts on Z^d, and M(beta)=(q mu_beta^1(sigma_0=1)-1)/(q-1), beta_c=inf{beta:M(beta)>0}. Seek delta,r0,b>0,C>=0, independent of beta and volume, so every beta_c<beta<beta_c+delta with 0<M(beta)<r0 admits a differentiable F_beta(m)=a_beta m^2-b_beta m^3+R_beta(m), b_beta>=b, |R_beta|<=C m^4, |R_beta prime|<=4C m^3 on [0,r0], with F_beta prime(M(beta))=0 and F_beta(M(beta))<=F_beta(0)=0. Only the scalar mean-field entropy special case is established. The lattice input, particularly q=d=3, remains unproved.
assumptions: unproved proposed input for the actual lattice model
uniform constants and physical stationarity/minimum link

entries.title: DRAFT: uniform cubic potential implies critical Potts ordering
entries.statement: CONDITIONAL REDUCTION ONLY, pending independent proof admission. For integer q,d>=3 and normalized monochromatic-boundary magnetization M(beta), assume the entire uniform-potential input stated in this bundle on (beta_c,beta_c+delta). The exclusion lemma gives M(beta)>=eta=min(r0,b/(6C)) for C>0, or eta=r0 for C=0. Finite-box magnetizations are continuous in beta and decrease with box size; their infimum M is upper semicontinuous and nondecreasing. Hence M is right-continuous at beta_c and M(beta_c)>=eta>0. The uniform-potential input is not proved, so C0048 is not solved.
assumptions: standard FK domain and parameter comparison
no conclusion without the unproved input
